messages:
andrew (platform-pm): quick q — before we flip an automatic fallback policy, can we surface a realtime preview of which requests would be affected? worried about blind spots (quota edge cases, multi-tenant routing).
maya (eng-ux): yes, a preview toggle seems helpful. are you thinking deterministic rules (exact match) or probabilistic scoring (e.g. confidence < 0.6 triggers)? :thinking_face:
jason (sre): also need to show how this interacts with per-customer quotas and reserved capacity. preview should flag requests that would be rate-limited differently if fallback applied.
li (platform): conceptually we can simulate routing decisions against a short window of live traffic. `simulate` could run against a sampling stream and return sample ids + decision reasons. e.g. `ri rollout simulate --policy autofb-23 --window 60s --sample 0.5`
li (platform): example output we could show in the UX: ```[ {"req_id": "r-12345", "route": "chat-gpt-ish", "latency_ms": 145, "decision": "fallback", "reason": "model-500-spike"}, {"req_id": "r-12346", "route": "embeddings", "decision": "keep", "reason": "quota-exempt"} ]```
andrew (platform-pm): perfect — show me counts by route + percent of customer impact. we should surface both absolute affected QPS and percent of total for each tenant.
sarah (product): tiny UX ask — make it obvious when the preview is based on sampled traffic vs full replay. sampling can under/over-estimate noise. :warning:
maya (eng-ux): agreed. UI proposal: top banner: "Preview mode — sampled at 1% (approx 4k reqs/min). Click \"Run full replay\" to run a replay on stored traces." then a table with columns: route, impacted_qps_est, pct_traffic, top_reasons (tag cloud), example_req_id.
jason (sre): replay will be expensive. we should add TTL and cost estimate before users run full replays. Also require ops approval for cross-tenant replays.
li (platform): implementation note: we need to attach a deterministic decision trace id to each simulated decision for auditability, e.g., `decision_trace: dt-20231105-0001`. That ID must correlate to telemetry logs and to rollout config version.
ops-bot: Note: Replay jobs require `team-ops` approval if they exceed 10m requests. See https://internal.docs/replay-rules
andrew (platform-pm): on the UI, include a small inline diff comparing current live routing vs post-policy routing — highlight routes that flip often (oscillation risk). maybe a risk score.
maya (eng-ux): risk score idea: combine oscillation (freq of flips in preview), percent_impact, and confidence on signal source. display as Low/Medium/High with hover tooltip.
sarah (product): for canary rollouts we should support a "what-if" that restricts policy to a subset of tenants (by tag) and surface which tenants would see the change. that way sales/customers can be excluded.
jason (sre): edge-case: if a tenant is on dedicated capacity, autofallback may be disabled; preview must mark those as "not applicable" instead of implying no impact.
li (platform): good catch — we also need to simulate quota interplay: e.g., fallback may increase token consumption elsewhere. preview should run a simple cost model and show expected tokens/sec.
andrew (platform-pm): auditability: every preview/run should persist a short snapshot (policy version, args, sample rate, decision_trace ids) for 90d. auditors should be able to pull the snapshot id and replay it server-side.
maya (eng-ux): what about showing example traced spans so SREs can quickly open relevant traces? clicking an example_req_id should open the trace view with the decision_trace pre-filter.
jason (sre): yes. ensure PII redaction in trace preview. also mark requests that were proxied to fallback models with a suffix so logs/traces can be filtered. e.g., `route: chat@fallback-v2`
andrew (platform-pm): next steps: li — prototype simulation CLI output. maya — mockups for header banners + risk score. jason/sarah — define legal/ops guardrails for cross-tenant replays. i'll schedule a 30m sync after prototypes. :+1:
li (platform): will do, starting with a cheap sample-based implementation. expect a draft by EOD Fri.
maya (eng-ux): mockups incoming. leaning toward a small modal to avoid clutter.
sarah (product): adding product review to the calendar invite.
ops-bot: Action created: replay-approval-request-445 (assignee: team-ops)
andrew (platform-pm): thanks everyone — objective is that turning on autofallback shouldn't be a surprise for customers. preview + clear audit trail should be enough to move faster.
